name: Mathematics (Min)

rules.name: Minor Requirements

children.name: Three of the six at the 100 level and above
The other three: Math courses at or above MATH 51
100-level and above courses taken at Stanford

rules.desc:
• The Math minor consists of six math courses at or above Math 51.

• Minors must complete at least three 100-level and above courses within the six math courses

• STATS116 (No longer offered), STATS118 or STATS200 (at most one, but not both and neither if STATS116 is being used), PHIL 151, PHIL 152 count as 100-level math courses for the Math minor requirement. No other courses outside the Math Department can count in this way. There are no exceptions to this for any reason.

• MATH 190, MATH 193, MATH 193X, MATH 197, MATH 198, and MATH 199 cannot count toward the minor

• All 100-level and above courses must be taken at Stanford.

• Only Math 50/60CM/60DM series and first-year calculus can be double counted toward any other major or minor

rules.name: Recommended (NOT REQUIRED) Courses
rules.desc:
It is recommended (but not required) that the six courses towards the minor include one multivariable mathematics series:

• MATH51, MATH52, MATH53.

• MATH61CM, MATH62CM, MATH63CM.

• MATH61DM, MATH62DM, MATH63DM.

gpa: All courses counted toward the minor must receive a grade of B- or above.
grading: All courses counted toward the minor must be taken for a letter grade.
transferPolicy:
External credit may be used toward only Math courses below the 100-level.
External credit must be approved by the university Registrar’s Office and listed in MAP before it can be used towards the minor requirements.
See the transfer credit process on the Math department website for information about the process to request approval: https://mathematics.stanford.edu/academicsundergraduate-studentsmath-major/transfer-credit-process
reviewNotes: The audit checks six Math courses numbered 51 or above, at least three of them at the 100 level, with STATS 116, 118 or 200 counting as one 100-level Math course (at most one of them). Every course must be letter graded with a B- or better. Checked by hand: that your 100-level courses were taken at Stanford (outside credit counts only below the 100 level), two more courses the Bulletin counts as 100-level, and six excluded courses the Bulletin names without a number.
